answer: I would build the whole defence on Stone sawyer lintel seal carved into the stone yard ledger: each lintel is a measured stone yield plus a guild signature, so a mason must saw a, and no faster road exists. One proof costs 110 POA; 429 proofs cost 47190 POA, and the farm must pay before it earns anything. The ridge names the issuer, the fable names the price, and the sonnet names the date: a forger must forge all three. Templates die here: every proof is per identity and every price is per alias.
